items.title: How can AI accelerate the green transition?
items.abstract: In his essay The Gift, published in 1925, the sociologist Marcel Mauss emphasised the 'total' scope of the phenomenon of gift-and counter-gift-giving, noting that it 'expresses, simultaneously and all at once, all manner of institutions: religious, legal and moral (...)\,; economic (...)\,; not to mention the aesthetic phenomena to which these facts give rise (...).'' The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), which is suddenly and profoundly disrupting individual and collective lives, bears a resemblance to the ''total social fact'' described a hundred years ago. AI refers to technologies designed to simulate human intelligence, namely an ''automated system that (...) deduces, from received inputs, how to generate output results such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that may influence physical or virtual environments.'' 4 (OECD). Having become central to human relations, AI relies on physical and globalised infrastructure and therefore, also has an impact on the environment. This paper analyses some of these effects and how they are perceived by society. This text offers an exploration of the links between AI and the ecological transition, seeking to identify new opportunities and constraints. To this end, it will identify the barriers to the ecological transition (1) and the environmental impacts attributable to AI (2). It will then go on to describe how to live in a constrained world (3) while AI accelerates scientific discovery (4) and profoundly transforms society (5).

items.title: Human Factors in Aircraft Maintenance: Linking Occupational Motivation, Work Alienation, and Flow Experience
items.abstract: Today's aviation maintenance environments place significant cognitive and psychological demands on aircraft maintenance technicians due to increasing fleet size, intense operational pace, and extremely low tolerance for error. In this context, understanding the psychological and motivational processes that shape the human performance of maintenance personnel is critical for the sustainability of flight safety. This study aims to examine the relationships between work alienation, occupational motivation, and work-related flow in aircraft maintenance technicians within a holistic model framework. The research was conducted using data from 207 aircraft maintenance technicians. Descriptive and correlational analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics (version 31). The proposed research model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) via the SEM module of Jamovi (version 2.7.6) software and the lavaan package running in the R environment. The mediating role of occupational motivation was evaluated using the bootstrap resampling method. The findings show that work alienation significantly and negatively affects occupational motivation and work-related flow experience; while occupational motivation positively predicts work-related flow. Mediation analyses revealed that occupational motivation plays a partial mediating role in the relationship between work alienation and work-related flow. The results indicate that human performance in maintenance settings should be considered not only from the perspective of technical competence and error management, but also by taking into account motivation and psychological attachment processes.

items.title: Human Factors in Data Preparation
items.abstract: Data preparation is a cornerstone of the data science lifecycle, yet it remains one of the most time-consuming and human-dependent stages. Human factors are critical here, shaping how users interact with tools, perceive data quality, and make trade-offs under uncertainty. At the crossroads of Human–Computer Interaction (HCI), Visualization, and human-in/over-the-loop paradigms, recent research highlights new opportunities to make data preparation more usable, transparent, and trustworthy. Interactive interfaces and visual analytics systems allow users to iteratively refine transformations, explore provenance, and detect anomalies, while cognitive aspects such as workload, bias, and trust determine the reliability of human interventions. Automation increasingly complements these workflows: human-in-the-loop methods leverage user feedback to guide cleaning, labeling, or schema alignment, and over-the-loop frameworks provide oversight mechanisms to prevent over-reliance on automation. At the same time, modern generative AI introduces powerful new capabilities, such as automatically suggesting transformations, synthesizing metadata or documentation, and even generating realistic synthetic datasets. These advances promise efficiency and creativity but raise concerns about reliability, explainability, and provenance, reinforcing the need for careful human oversight. This chapter reviews these possibilities and the research challenges in developing a new class of hybrid, adaptive data-preparation solutions that blend human expertise with automated intelligence. Key challenges include balancing scalability with user effort, ensuring transparency in automated suggestions, preventing loss of situational awareness, and developing evaluation metrics that reflect both human experience and technical accuracy. Addressing these challenges will enable more robust, human-aware data preparation practices across domains.

items.title: Human–AI symbiosis for resilient supply chains: a Delphi-fuzzy cognitive mapping analysis of an Indian textile sector
items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can augment rather than replace human decision-making in human-centric supply chains, and how this synergy enhances supply chain flexibility (SCF) and supply chain resilience (SCR), using a textile sector in North India as the real-world context. Design/methodology/approach The study is conducted in two phases. The first phase focuses on identifying and prioritizing the relevant AI-related and human-centric factors for the study, which is addressed through an exhaustive literature review for identification and then the Delphi method to prioritize them. The second phase focuses on modeling the relationship between these factors using fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) approach. Expert inputs are used to construct the causal structure and analyze the strength of interconnections. By modeling bidirectional and nonlinear relationships rather than assuming static, unidirectional causality, this method captures feedback dynamics, which conventional linear techniques cannot represent. Findings The results show that human-centric factors particularly human–AI augmentation, human–machine collaboration and workforce preparedness play a central role in translating AI capabilities into SCF and SCR. AI-related factors primarily act as drivers, while supply chain outcomes materialize through these human-centric mechanisms. Originality/value This study offers a mechanism-based explanation of AI-enabled supply chain performance and employs FCM to capture complex interrelationships within a sociotechnical system.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Systems That Prioritize and Enhance Human Intelligence
items.abstract: In a world of accelerating change, there is a need for wise and adaptive human reasoning. Integrating AI capabilities with human guidance offers promise, though human reasoning itself is often hasty, shortsighted, and error-prone, and no clear framework exists for combining human reasoning strategies with AI across diverse tasks. This article proposes a framework for human-centered hybrid reasoning systems that engage and enhance human reasoning abilities ranging from granular data analysis to high-level reflection and wisdom. The framework was developed through a conceptual synthesis combining: (1) established strategies for enhancing human reasoning, (2) AI design approaches that favor pre-conclusive engagement over the generation of conclusions, and (3) the treatment of reasoning as a collection of distinct, individually supportable modes. This synthesis produced a distinctive framework for broad-spectrum reasoning enhancement from which a typology of reasoning modes, a system architecture, and a high-level research agenda were derived.

items.title: Identifying Workflow Bottlenecks in Virtual Reality Personal Protective Equipment Simulation
items.abstract: Existing personal protective equipment (PPE) research in virtual reality (VR) has primarily examined overall training effectiveness. To inform design optimization, this study identified segment-level interaction hotspots in a CDC-informed head-mounted display VR PPE scenario. Thirty-nine participants completed a six-segment donning and doffing workflow using handheld controllers. Segment completion time and video-coded additional user action (AUA) counts were analyzed using repeated-measures statistics and participant-clustered generalized estimating equations, with negative binomial and mixed-effects sensitivity analyses. Platform or system anomalies were coded and reported separately from AUA counts. Both measures differed significantly across segments. Gloves-and-goggles doffing was the primary combined hotspot, showing the largest time ratio and AUA incidence rate ratio relative to gown donning, whereas goggles donning was the principal donning-specific hotspot. These findings indicate that interaction burden was concentrated in specific segments of the implemented workflow. Segment-aware redesign may improve usability and interaction efficiency in VR PPE systems.

items.title: Impact of Multimedia Display Technologies on Visual Fatigue and Learning Effectiveness
items.abstract: The rapid transition from traditional to digital education has significantly transformed teaching and learning processes. Modern classrooms are now equipped with multimedia technologies such as interactive boards, projectors, and internet-enabled tools, making education more flexible and accessible. However, the excessive use of digital technology has introduced new challenges, particularly digital fatigue among students. Digital fatigue is characterized by mental exhaustion resulting from prolonged screen exposure, repetitive digital content consumption, and limited face-to-face interaction. The increasing reliance on digital platforms has been associated with reduced motivation, lower efficiency, and heightened stress among students. Prolonged screen use can also lead to physiological issues such as headaches, eye irritation, difficulty concentrating, and sleep disturbances, commonly referred to as digital eye strain. In addition to physical effects, digital learning environments contribute to psychological challenges, including anxiety, emotional exhaustion, and burnout, which negatively affect students’ academic performance and overall well-being. Sleep disruption further exacerbates these problems, as excessive screen time interferes with rest and recovery. Moreover, the lack of clear boundaries between academic and personal time in digital settings can result in continuous mental strain. The physical classroom environment also plays a crucial role, as factors such as improper lighting, glare, and poor viewing distances can intensify visual discomfort and fatigue. While multimedia technologies enhance interactivity and accessibility in education, their unregulated use may adversely affect students’ cognitive, visual, and emotional health. Despite the implementation of hybrid learning models, there remains a need for more structured and effective strategies to address digital fatigue. This study highlights the importance of promoting digital well-being through balanced technology use, ergonomic practices, and improved classroom design.

items.title: Incipit: Axiom-Grounded Scaffolding for Human-AI Literary Creation
items.abstract: Large language models can produce fluent prose from short prompts, but direct prompt-to-text interaction gives writers limited access to the assumptions that shape a long narrative. We present Incipit, an implemented research prototype that introduces an explicit planning layer between a writer's intent and generated prose. This layer is grounded in literary axioms, defined as curated and reusable propositions about human experience and narrative craft. The prototype connects a knowledge base of 1455 axioms and 472 typed relationships with a five-round direction dialogue, a retrieval-and-selection pipeline, and a three-level blueprint covering creative premises, story beats and character arcs, and chapter outlines. Writers can inspect and edit these structures before using them as context for scene generation. Additional modules support real-event abstraction and five-dimensional diagnostic feedback. We describe the system design rationale, data flow, implementation boundaries, and a worked design example. As no controlled user study or independently rated output study has yet been completed, we do not claim that the system improves literary quality. Instead, we outline a future preregistered evaluation designed to distinguish the contribution of axiom grounding from that of hierarchical planning. The paper contributes a concrete architecture for using literary knowledge as an inspectable coordination object in human-AI writing.

items.title: Incremental effects of passive stretching added to device-based massage on lower-limb range of motion and neuromuscular response in sedentary adults
items.abstract: Prolonged sitting restricts lower-limb joint mobility, and conventional device-based massage has limited capacity to expand joint range of motion (ROM). This study examined whether adding a passive stretching module to device-based massage produces additional immediate lower-limb improvements. Forty-one sedentary adults were randomly assigned to two groups: the main group completed conventional massage (CON) followed, in a fixed order, by passive-stretch massage (PST), while an independent control group repeated CON twice. The PST phase produced significantly greater immediate incremental ROM gains than repeated CON across hip flexion, abduction, extension and knee flexion. Target-muscle %MVC remained below 5% throughout PST, with iEMG 62-79% lower than CON and subjective ratings indicated positive relaxation, flexibility improvement and willingness to continue use. These immediate, single-session findings offer preliminary support for integrating passive stretching into device-based massage systems; long-term effects and practical application value warrant further investigation.

items.title: Influence of Parenting Styles on Sports Performance among Student-athletes of Lead City University, Ibadan
items.abstract: Sports performance among student-athletes is influenced by their families in addition to their physical, technical and mental abilities. While negative or excessively controlling parenting styles may result in stress and decreased performance, positive parental involvement may promote resilience, self-esteem and commitment. This study investigated the influence of parenting styles on sports performance among student-athletes of Lead City University, Ibadan. Descriptive survey research design was used. The population was all student-athletes of Lead City University (LCU), Ibadan. The sample size was 102 student-athletes with convenience sampling technique. Standardised instruments of the Parenting Style Scale and Sports Performance Perception Scale were modified and used to collect data. The Cronbach's alpha method was used for internal consistency. Reliability coefficients of the instruments were 0.89 and 0.86. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyse the data. The results indicated that there was no significant joint influence of parenting style (F(3,98)=0.935, p>0.05) on sports performance among the student-athletes. There was no significant relative influence of authoritative parenting style (β=0.048, p>0.05), authoritarian parenting style (β=0.156, p>0.05) and permissive parenting style (β=0.014, p>0.05) on sports performance. It was concluded that parenting styles do not significantly influence athletes’ sports performance at this stage; parenting styles may have little impact on their performance, and other factors, such as coaching quality, peer support and personal motivation, are likely more influential. Based on the conclusion, it was recommended that undergraduate athletes should be encouraged to develop self-discipline, intrinsic motivation and personal goal-setting skills.

While negative or excessively controlling parenting styles may result in stress and decreased performance, positive parental involvement may promote resilience, self-esteem and commitment. This study investigated the influence of parenting styles on sports performance among student-athletes of Lead City University, Ibadan. Descriptive survey research design was used. The population was all student-athletes of Lead City University (LCU), Ibadan. The sample size was 102 student-athletes with convenience sampling technique. Standardised instruments of the Parenting Style Scale and Sports Performance Perception Scale were modified and used to collect data. The Cronbach's alpha method was used for internal consistency. Reliability coefficients of the instruments were 0.89 and 0.86. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyse the data. The results indicated that there was no significant joint influence of parenting style (F(3,98)=0.935, p>0.05) on sports performance among the student-athletes. There was no significant relative influence of authoritative parenting style (β=0.048, p>0.05), authoritarian parenting style (β=0.156, p>0.05) and permissive parenting style (β=0.014, p>0.05) on sports performance. It was concluded that parenting styles do not significantly influence athletes’ sports performance at this stage; parenting styles may have little impact on their performance, and other factors, such as coaching quality, peer support and personal motivation, are likely more influential. Based on the conclusion, it was recommended that undergraduate athletes should be encouraged to develop self-discipline, intrinsic motivation and personal goal-setting skills.

items.title: Inside the Mind of the Prosumer
items.abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) represent a promising pathway for citizen engagement in the energy transition, yet their adoption in Poland remains limited despite the nation’s recent individual-driven photovoltaic boom. From a behavioral economics perspective, this Polish experience offers valuable empirical insights for evidence-based green transition policies. This chapter investigates the psychological, social, and systemic factors shaping individuals’ readiness to join RECs. Using mixed methods integrating 30 in-depth stakeholder interviews and a nationwide survey of 974 Polish prosumers, this study provides a multi-level analysis of the challenge. Qualitative analysis reveals how systemic barriers, including legislative instability and deep-seated institutional distrust rooted in Poland’s socio-historical context, translate into individual fears of financial risk and social conflict. Quantitative results show that participation intentions are shaped more by psychological dispositions such as personal values, pro-environmental attitudes, and digital engagement than by traditional socio-demographic factors. These findings underscore that REC adoption is driven by complex subjective motivations and perceived systemic friction that significantly exceeds simple economic rationale. The chapter concludes with strategic implications emphasizing targeted, value-congruent communication strategies and sociotechnical systems designed to build trust and reduce psychological transaction costs. These behavioral insights can inform evidence-based green transition policies that account for the psychological and social dynamics underlying citizen participation in sustainable energy initiatives.

items.title: Inteligencia Artificial con Alma: Modelo Humanista para una Transformación Digital Ética, Confiable y Orientada al Bienestar
items.abstract: Objective: To formulate and substantiate the “Artificial Intelligence with Soul” model as a humanistic framework for governing, designing, adopting, and evaluating artificial intelligence systems in organizations and universities. Methodology: A theoretical-propositional study was conducted through an integrative review of literature on trustworthy artificial intelligence, algorithmic ethics, human-centered design, sociotechnical systems, digital well-being, data justice, explainability, human oversight, and risk management. International regulatory and technical frameworks were compared, including UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. Results: A multilevel model is proposed comprising six principles—legitimate purpose, dignity and rights, human agency, justice and inclusion, sociotechnical trustworthiness, and sustainable well-being—four governance layers—strategic, organizational, technical, and relational—and a 4A activation cycle: Learning, Attitude, Soul, and Action. The article contributes an assessment matrix, twelve testable propositions, an indicator dashboard, a preliminary 36-item scale, and an implementation roadmap. Conclusions: Responsible AI cannot be reduced to regulatory compliance or technical accuracy. It requires alignment among purpose, data, architecture, decisions, power relations, and human consequences. The model translates ethical principles into verifiable practices and offers a research agenda for validating its usefulness across sectors and cultural contexts.

items.title: Internal and External Factors in Reading Performance Among Grade 1 Learners
items.abstract: This study examines the internal and external factors influencing the reading proficiency of Grade 1 learners at Babag 1 Elementary School in Lapu-Lapu City. Using a descriptive-correlational and causal-comparative research design, data were collected from 100 parents through a researcher-made survey questionnaire measuring socio-economic profile and perceived factors affecting reading proficiency. Results revealed that most parents belong to the lower-middle income bracket, with smartphones as the most available learning device. Teacher-provided reading tasks emerged as the strongest external factor, while decoding skills were the primary internal strength among learners, although motivation for leisure reading remained limited. Most pupils performed at a “Satisfactory” level in reading. Correlation analysis showed that both internal and external factors significantly relate to reading performance; however, regression findings indicated that only internal factors significantly predict reading proficiency. These results highlighted that strengthening young learners’ intrinsic motivation, attention, and engagement in reading is more influential than socio-economic support alone. Lastly, an action plan is crafted and recommended for implementation to foster lifelong reading interest.

items.title: Interpersonal Interaction in AR Mediated Informal Learning on Cultural Relics: The Effects of Goal, Asymmetry, Competition, and Proxemics
items.abstract: Interpersonal interaction is crucial for informal learning on cultural relics. This study investigates how four factors - mutual goals, asymmetric interaction, competitive interaction, and interpersonal distance - affect collaborative learning and collective experience. Through an empirical emperiment (N = 70) analyzing self-report, gaze, and physiological data, the study found that mutual goals, asymmetric interaction and competitive interaction enhanced collective experience, whereas interpersonal distance had minimal impact. Mutual goals reduced psychological stress and common gaze, suggesting that coordination decreased reliance on vision. However, asymmetric and competitive interactions negatively affected learning performance, likely due to the uneven distribution of information and cognitive resource consumption. Close interpersonal distance promoted concentration and emotional stability, but not learning performance. Crucially, findings reveal a structural tension in AR-mediated learning: while interpersonal interaction increased engagement and collaborative satisfaction, they introduce attentional noise that hinders individual deep content processing. The study provides a theoretical and empirical basis for designing collaborative AR systems in the cultural heritage contexts.

items.title: INVESTIGATING EFL STUDENTS’ ENGAGEMENT IN GENAI-BASED COLLABORATIVE INQUIRY FOR DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING IN ARGUMENTATIVE WRITING
items.abstract: This study aims to investigate EFL students’ engagement in GenAI-based collaborative inquiry for developing critical thinking in argumentative writing. It employed a descriptive qualitative research design that involved 14 third-semester undergraduate students from the English Education Study Program at STIT Miftahul Midad Lumajang who participated in collaborative argumentative writing tasks supported by GenAI tools. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis to examine students’ engagement processes and the role of GenAI in their collaborative writing activities. The findings reveal that students’ engagement is reflected through three interconnected themes, namely cognitive engagement through idea development and critical thinking, social engagement through collaborative interaction, and reflective engagement through AI-mediated feedback. These findings further indicate that GenAI serves as a mediational tool that facilitates not only idea development but also collaborative dialogue and metacognitive awareness. Variations in students’ reliance on AI and their participation patterns highlight the need for pedagogical guidance to ensure meaningful engagement. Overall, the study suggests that integrating GenAI into collaborative inquiry can provide opportunities for students to promote active participation, critical evaluation, and reflective thinking in EFL writing contexts.

items.title: Kajian Antropometri Kaki Perempuan Bandung dengan Profesi Beraktivitas Tinggi dalam Berdiri dan Berjalan
items.abstract: A mismatch between shoe sizes and the foot anthropometric characteristics of Indonesian women can cause discomfort and affect shoe fit, particularly for women whose daily activities involve significant standing and walking. This study aims to identify the foot anthropometric characteristics of women in Bandung who engage in high levels of standing and walking and to analyze how these characteristics align with shoe sizing systems currently on the market. The study employed an anthropometric approach involving direct measurements of 100 Indonesian female respondents aged 18–35 years with high levels of standing and walking activity. Measured dimensions included foot length, foot width, instep circumference, mid-foot height, heel-ankle circumference, ankle circumference, and arch height. Data were analyzed using normality tests, uniformity tests, data adequacy tests, descriptive statistics, and comparative analysis against commercial shoe sizing systems. The results indicate that the respondents' feet had an average length of 24 cm and an average width of 9.13 cm. Comparisons with commercial sizing standards revealed a discrepancy in foot length of 2.49–3.09 cm within the EU size range of 38–42, suggesting a tendency toward over-sizing in commercially available shoes. The "Japan Size 24.0 cm" system most closely matched the respondents' average foot length, although its application would still require adjustments to account for local anthropometric characteristics. Therefore, the development of shoe sizing standards based on the foot anthropometry of Indonesian women and the design of a master shoe last incorporating a 10–15 mm allowance are recommended to produce footwear that is more ergonomic, comfortable, and better suited to user characteristics

items.title: Knowledge of Malaria Transmission, Treatment Adherence, and Antimalarial Drug Resistance Awareness among Adults in Osun State, Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major public health burden in Nigeria, driven by biological and modifiable human factors. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of malaria transmission, treatment, and drug resistance among adults in Osun State, Nigeria, and examined associations between cognitive gaps and preventive/treatment-seeking behaviors using the Health Belief Model. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,500 adults (≥18 years) in Osun State between June and August 2023 using a pre-tested questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used. Key gaps: 49.5% were unaware of the primary transmission route, and only 27.5% recognized antimalarial drug resistance. Among 712 participants who used antimalarial drugs in the past two weeks, 70.5% completed treatment. Awareness of drug resistance was independently associated with treatment completion (aOR=1.68; 95% CI:1.25–2.25; p<0.001), formal healthcare use (aOR=1.45; 95% CI:1.12–1.88; p=0.005), and lower herbal medicine use (aOR=0.65; 95% CI:0.50–0.85; p=0.002). Female gender predicted insecticide-treated net use (aOR=2.15; 95% CI:1.65–2.80; p<0.001) but was inversely associated with drug resistance awareness (aOR=0.62; 95% CI:0.46–0.83; p=0.001). Knowledge deficits, especially regarding drug resistance, are linked to less favourable preventive and treatment-seeking behaviours. items.title: Large Language Models for Test-Enhanced Learning: A Tutorial and Proof of Concept
items.abstract: Practice tests improve retention of studied information and enhance learning and retrieval of new information (test-enhanced learning; TEL). In five preregistered studies (total N = 623)—four online randomized experiments and one correlational classroom study with final-year psychology undergraduates—we examined whether large language models (LLMs; Gemini and ChatGPT) can generate practice tests that promote TEL and whether this use of LLMs can be feasibly incorporated into a classroom setting. LLM-generated multiple-choice tests with fixed feedback did not improve 2-day recall of a TED Talk relative to a control (Studies 1 and 2). In contrast, LLM-generated short-answer tests with personalized feedback significantly improved 7-day recall of an educational video relative to rewatching it (Studies 3 and 4), regardless of whether final test format matched that of the practice test. In the classroom study, participation in fortnightly LLM-generated short-answer tests (with personalized feedback) on lecture content was positively associated with graded assessment performance, and students’ attitudes towards this use of LLMs were generally favorable. Overall, we demonstrate that LLMs can substantially reduce the practical burden of implementing TEL, while maintaining sufficiently good question quality and enabling automated personalized feedback, and that this approach can be feasibly deployed in an undergraduate psychology class.

items.title: Learners’ Environmental Condition and Motivation: Its Relation to Academic Performance
items.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between learners’ environmental conditions, motivation, and academic performance among selected learners during the 1st quarter of the school year 2025–2026. Specifically, it examined the respondents’ demographic profile in terms of age, sex, parents’ occupation, and number of siblings, as well as environmental factors influencing learner motivation, including classroom conditions, availability of learning materials, teacher-student relationships, home study environment, and noise levels and distractions. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed, with a sample of 100 respondents. The findings revealed that learners generally perceived their environment positively, with strong agreement regarding classroom conditions, teacher- student relationships, and home support, while noise and distractions were moderately disruptive. Academic performance was moderate, with the majority of respondents achieving fairly satisfactory to satisfactory grades. Correlation and regression analyses indicated that environmental factors and demographic characteristics were not significantly related to academic performance. The study concluded that while environmental conditions and support systems were important for engagement, other factors, such as intrinsic motivation, self-regulation, and study habits, play a more critical role in academic achievement. The findings suggested a need for a holistic approach that combines environmental improvements with strategies to enhance learners’ personal motivation and learning skills.

items.title: LEME: open large language models for ophthalmology with advanced reasoning and clinical validation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer potential to alleviate the growing public health burden of eye disease; however, few models have been tailored for ophthalmology or evaluated against clinically relevant benchmarks and real-world workflows. Here, we present LEME, a suite of open-weight LLMs for ophthalmology developed via a two-stage framework: instruction tuning on 211,149 examples curated from authoritative sources, and reinforcement learning with 29,747 preference-labeled examples to enhance clinical reasoning and informativeness. LEME was evaluated under zero-shot settings using five curated benchmarks, covering question answering and patient-physician consultation. LEME outperformed all seven baselines (all p < 0.004), notably exceeding GPT-4o by 3.32% in average ROUGE-L. Furthermore, LEME was assessed on three downstream tasks using deidentified patient data. In answering patient queries, LEME received the highest overall ratings from attending clinicians; its completeness rating even surpassed that of the expert-written answers ( p = 0.015). For visual acuity extraction from clinical notes, LEME achieved the highest F1 scores, outperforming LLaMA-3 70B by 14.1% and Eye-LLaMA by 59.0%. Finally, in assessment and treatment plan generation, LEME achieved ratings approaching those of attending clinicians, demonstrating promise for ophthalmic decision support. All models, datasets, and code are made open to support further development and validation.

items.title: Lightweight UAV-based object detection and tracking for intelligent oil and gas field safety monitoring
items.abstract: Continuous, reliable monitoring of geographically dispersed oil and gas production facilities is essential for accident prevention, asset integrity, and regulatory compliance, yet ground-based inspection is labour-intensive and temporally sparse. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer on-demand aerial coverage, but automated interpretation of production-site imagery is hindered by extreme target-scale variation, irregular equipment geometries, and the limited compute available on airborne platforms. This paper presents an integrated lightweight detection-and-tracking framework tailored to oil and gas field surveillance. The detector augments YOLOv8s with deformable C2f (DCNv2) modules for geometry-adaptive feature extraction, a progressive feature pyramid (AFPN) that suppresses cross-scale semantic conflict, a parameter-shared detail-enhanced head (LSDECD-Head), a Focaler-GIoU regression loss, and LAMP structured pruning for embedded deployment. For dynamic situational awareness, an improved ByteTrack introduces a spatial-appearance similarity matrix encoding operational-state cues and an acceleration-aware Kalman correction. On VisDrone2019, UAVDT, and a self-constructed oil-and-gas dataset (OGF-UAV), the method attains 44.1%, 57.6%, and 56.3% mAP@0.5 with only 7.8 M parameters at 78 FPS, and reduces tracking identity switches by up to 43.2%. The pruned model runs at 18.3 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16 GB under TensorRT FP16, confirming practicality for real-time field deployment.

items.title: LLMs can assist with proposal selection at large user facilities
items.abstract: Abstract We explore how large language models (LLMs) can enhance the proposal selection process at large user facilities, offering a scalable, consistent, and cost-effective alternative to traditional human review. Proposal selection depends on assessing the relative strength among submitted proposals; however, traditional human scoring often suffers from weak inter-proposal correlations and is subject to reviewer bias and inconsistency. A pairwise preference-based approach is logically superior, providing a more rigorous and internally consistent basis for ranking, but its quadratic workload makes it impractical for human reviewers. We address this limitation using LLMs. Leveraging the uniquely well-curated proposals and publication records from three beamlines at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), we show that the LLM rankings correlate strongly with the human rankings (Spearman $$\rho \simeq 0.2-0.8$$ , improving to $$\ge 0.5$$ after 10% outlier removal). Moreover, LLM performance is no worse than that of human reviewers in identifying proposals with high publication potential, while costing over two orders of magnitude less. Beyond ranking, LLMs enable advanced analyses that are challenging for humans, such as quantitative assessment of proposal similarity via embedding models, which provides information crucial for review committees.

items.title: Longitudinal associations of occupational cumulative noise exposure duration and hearing loss with lipid profiles: a 9-year cohort study
items.abstract: Background Occupational noise exposure causes auditory damage and is also closely associated with systemic metabolic abnormalities. The impact of long-term noise exposure on longitudinal lipid changes remains unclear. Objective This longitudinal study examined the association of baseline cumulative noise exposure duration with serum triglycerides (TG) and total cholesterol (TC) in male workers, and further examined whether binaural high-frequency average hearing threshold (BHFTA), an objective marker of noise-induced cochlear damage, modified longitudinal lipid trends. Methods In this retrospective longitudinal cohort study, 431 male workers were followed for 9 years. Occupational noise exposure was defined according to the Chinese national standard GBZ/T 224-2010 as exposure to an 8-hour equivalent continuous A-weighted sound level of at least 80 dB(A) (Lex, 8h), and was operationalized as the cumulative duration of employment in noise-exposed positions ascertained from plant administrative records. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the effects of follow-up time, baseline cumulative noise exposure duration (mean-centered, time-invariant), and their interaction on natural log-transformed TG and TC, adjusted for age, body mass index, lipid-lowering medication use, smoking, and alcohol consumption. Simple slopes were estimated at representative exposure durations (3, 10, and 20 years). Because individual biological noise dose could not be directly measured, BHFTA was used as an objective marker of accumulated biological dose and individual susceptibility in sensitivity analyses, with simple slopes estimated at BHFTA values of mean ± 1 standard deviation (SD). Results Baseline cumulative noise exposure duration was significantly and positively associated with serum TG levels, with each additional year of exposure corresponding to an approximately 2.0% higher TG level (β = 0.0203 per year on ln(TG), 95% CI: 0.0029–0.0377, P = 0.022), whereas its association with TC did not reach statistical significance ( P = 0.077). The follow-up time and baseline exposure duration interaction was negative in direction, that is, the annual rate of lipid increase tended to be smaller among workers with longer baseline exposure; this reached borderline significance for TG (β = −0.0013, 95% CI: −0.0027–0.0001, P = 0.066) and statistical non-significance for TC ( P = 0.479). The estimated annual TG increase displayed a monotonic descriptive gradient across baseline exposure duration of 3, 10, and 20 years (5.35%, 4.39%, and 3.03% per year, respectively). In sensitivity analyses, BHFTA interacted positively with follow-up time for both outcomes (TG: 0.0023, 95% CI: 0.0013–0.0034; TC: 0.0005, 95% CI: 0.0001–0.0009); the estimated annual increase rose from 2.07 to 4.61% for TG and from 0.73 to 1.28% for TC as BHFTA increased from mean – 1 SD to mean + 1 SD (14.3–24.9 dB). Conclusions Baseline cumulative noise exposure duration was associated with elevated TG levels, and the attenuated rate of lipid increase over time may partly reflect a healthy worker survivor effect. In contrast, BHFTA may be more sensitive than administrative exposure records in revealing the metabolic consequences of chronic noise exposure. Hearing conservation and metabolic monitoring should be integrated into occupational health surveillance.

items.title: Managers Who Build and Managers Who Break: Abusive Supervision, Psychological Safety, and Team Learning-A Critical Review of the Evidence and Its Limits
items.abstract: In normal language, it's just one word that makes the difference between a manager and a damager, but the difference in behaviour between the two can be measured in the learning of the team, the health of the staff and the cost to the organisation. This article examines peer-reviewed journal evidence pertaining to supervisory behavior, including studies on abusive supervision, psychological safety, just culture in safety critical industries, and occupational health research that relates supervisors' ratings to reported illness. These can be found in occupational medicine cohort studies, regulatory text on error reporting and the use of data in the workplace, and in organisational behaviour journals and international standards on psychosocial risk. Three findings recur. First, teams which have leaders who ask how when things go wrong report more problems and make earlier corrections than teams with leaders who ask who. Second, hostile supervision is positively related to turnover intentions, decreased task performance and poorer health, with most designs being based on employee perception and there is limited ability to determine cause and effect. Third, the published figures of cost of damaging supervision are less convincing than the fact that they are frequently cited is sometimes thought to indicate. This article outlines the current measurement options, the legal parameters for their use, and practical options for employers, regulators, and employees. The evidence of causation and cross-country data are still relatively scarce.

items.title: Marker-Less Augmented Reality as a Catalyst for Digital Transformation in Furniture SMEs Through an Extension of the Cognitive–Affective–Conative Theory
items.abstract: While large firms of furniture industry have integrated technologies such as Augmented Reality (AR) to allow consumers to visualize 3D furniture in their own spaces before purchase, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have not yet fully optimized this technology. This study examines consumer acceptance of AR in the SME furniture sector by developing a prototype product catalog website that integrates AR functionality. It also introduces a new theoretical model, the Cognitive, Affective, Evaluative, Conative (CAEC) model, which extends the traditional Cognitive, Affective, Conative (CAC) theory by adding an evaluative stage. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining semi-structured interviews and surveys with the AR-enabled website prototype. The research contributes theoretically by introducing the CAEC model and provides a refined framework for understanding technology adoption. Practically, it guides SMEs in enhancing consumer engagement and purchase intentions through the use of AR.

items.title: Más Allá de la Salud: Modelo Integral de Felicidad, Bienestar y Florecimiento Humano
items.abstract: Objective: To substantiate a multidimensional model that expands health toward happiness, well-being, and flourishing by integrating personal, relational, material, and digital factors. Methodology: A theoretical-propositional study supported by an integrative review of the biopsychosocial model, subjective and eudaimonic well-being, self-determination, positive psychology, meaning, social determinants, capabilities, occupational health, and digital well-being. Results: The Integral Model of Human Well-Being with Soul (MIBHA) is formulated around eight dimensions—body, thought, emotions, transcendence, social life, professional life, finances, and technology—and five cross-cutting mechanisms: resources, agency, regulation, connection, and meaning. A theory of change, ten propositions, a preliminary 40-item scale, indicators, implementation phases, and ethical safeguards are developed. Conclusions: Well-being cannot be reduced to a score, an individual habit, or the absence of disease. It requires real capabilities, fair environments, and responsible governance. MIBHA offers a testable basis for research and intervention without replacing clinical diagnosis or treatment. Its original contribution lies in separating life domains from cross-cutting mechanisms, treating technology as a constitutive dimension, and introducing a non-compensation principle for severe deprivation.

items.title: Menopausal Symptom Burden and Self-Reported Poor Sleep Quality Among Japanese Working Women Aged 40 Years and Older: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Sleep-related complaints are common among women in midlife and may reflect not only insufficient sleep duration but also broader menopausal symptom burden. Although menopausal symptoms and sleep problems are known to be related, less is known about how menopausal symptom domains are associated with self-reported sleep quality among working women, particularly when objective sleep duration is considered. This exploratory cross-sectional study aimed to examine the association between menopausal symptom burden and self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older, while accounting for objectively measured sleep duration. Materials and Methods: Participants completed questionnaires on sleep quality and menopausal symptoms and underwent objective sleep monitoring using a wearable electroencephalography device. Self-reported sleep quality was assessed using an item corresponding to the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and dichotomized into poor and good sleep quality. Menopausal symptoms were evaluated using the Simplified Menopausal Index, including vasomotor, psychological, and somatic domains, with higher scores indicating greater symptom burden. Results: Among 79 participants, 43 reported poor sleep quality and 36 reported good sleep quality. Women with poor sleep quality had higher total and domain-specific SMI scores and shorter objective sleep duration. In logistic regression analyses adjusted for age and objective sleep duration, total SMI score and each symptom domain were associated with poor sleep quality. These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses excluding the sleep-related SMI item from the total score and psychological domain score. Conclusions: Self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older may reflect menopausal symptom burden beyond objectively measured sleep duration. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses supports the robustness of this association. Sleep complaints may therefore serve as an accessible signal for recognizing menopausal symptom burden in clinical and occupational health settings.

items.title: Migraine and related burden among employees of participating enterprises in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Migraine imposes a substantial burden on working-age populations, but evidence on migraine burden of industry category among enterprise employees remains limited. This study aimed to describe the proportion of employees meeting migraine criteria and migraine-related burden in a convenience sample of participating enterprises, and to explore their associations with industry category and measured work- and sleep-related characteristics. This cross-sectional study included 10,592 full-time employees, recruited from participating enterprises across 19 industry categories using multistage convenience sampling. Migraine was identified using the HARDSHIP questionnaire and clinical assessment according to ICHD-3 criteria. Sociodemographic factors, industry category, work schedule, sleep-related factors, migraine characteristics, disability, productivity loss, healthcare use, economic burden, coping behaviors, and social support were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with migraine. Among 10,592 employees, 2,792 participants met the study criteria for migraine, corresponding to an observed proportion of 26.36% in the analytic sample. The observed proportions differed across industry categories represented by the participating enterprises. Industry group was associated with migraine status after adjustment for the prespecified covariates. Insomnia frequency and later bedtime were consistently associated with higher observed migraine proportions across work-schedule groups, whereas patterns for night-shift frequency and working hours varied by work schedule. Participants with migraine reported substantial productivity loss, including reduced work efficiency, night-shift interruption, cancelled work-related activities, and limitations in family activities. Psychological distress, coping behaviors, and perceived social support also differed across industry category. Migraine represents an important occupational health concern among employees of participating enterprises, with its observed distribution and burden varying across occupational and work-schedule contexts. Workplace programs should integrate migraine recognition, access to care, sleep-health promotion, and appropriate scheduling accommodations. Prospective representative studies with detailed occupational exposures and clinical covariates are needed to confirm these associations and evaluate targeted interventions.

items.title: Morphological Characteristics and the Location-Dependent Variations of Thumb–Touchscreen Contact Areas in Two-Thumb Mobile Interaction
items.abstract: This study quantitatively investigated morphological characteristics of traces occurring between thumbs and touchscreen during two-thumb touch interaction on a mobile device. Thirty-two college students were recruited, and a paper-and-ink-based touch simulation using a mockup was conducted to capture thumb touch traces. Traces were collected at 22 target points on the virtual keyboard region, encompassing flexion–extension and abduction–adduction thumb movements, and the location-dependent variations in morphology were analyzed using major axis orientation, eccentricity, and area size (elliptical features). Results exhibited that during thumb displacement from flexion to extension, the major axes of the traces rotated clockwise for the left thumb and counterclockwise for the right, while the traces themselves became more circular and increased in size. In addition, during thumb excursion from abduction to adduction, the major axes of the traces generally rotated clockwise for the left thumb and counterclockwise for the right, while the traces became more elongated and showed no statistically significant change in area.

items.title: MOTIVATIONAL STRATEGIES OF SCIENCE TEACHERS AND STUDENT GRADE PERFORMANCE BASIS FOR INTERVENTION PROGRAM
items.abstract: The motivational strategies used by Science teachers and their relationship with students’ engagement and academic performance were assessed in this study as a basis for an intervention program. The study was conducted from June to November 2025. It examined teachers' use of intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies, students' behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement, their academic performance in Science, and their relationships. Quantitative descriptive-correlational research was conducted to 147 Grade 7 learners. Validated survey questionnaires and academic grade performance in Science were utilized to collect data. Descriptive statistics, such as the weighted mean and standard deviation, were used to characterize the variables, while Spearman’s rho was used to assess relationships among motivational strategies, student engagement, and academic grade performance. The results indicated that science teachers actively used extrinsic and intrinsic motivational strategies. Most students demonstrated behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement, and their first-quarter performance in Science showed strong academic competence. Furthermore, the intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies had a weak positive, statistically significant link with grade performance. However, no significant association was identified between the motivational strategies and students' behavioral, emotional, or cognitive engagement. The study indicates that motivational strategies have some impact on students’ academic performance, but the effect is very limited. The study led to the development of the Science Motivation and Engagement Enhancement Program (SMEEP) as an intervention to improve students’ motivation, engagement, and academic achievement in Science. The program involves intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies through well-organized pre-assessment, implementation, and post-assessment activities.

items.title: Multimodal Evaluation of Exoskeleton Assistance Using Optimized Machine Learning
items.abstract: Repetitive manual material handling (MMH) remains a leading occupational risk factor for work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSD), and passive shoulder-support exoskeletons have emerged as promising assistive technologies. Most evaluations rely on group-level statistics from single sensor modalities, leaving open whether their effects can be detected at the individual level. Thirty-five adults performed low-risk (4.54 kg, Lift Index (LI) < 1.0) lifting tasks, derived from the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation, with and without the passive shoulder exoskeleton support. Surface electromyography (sEMG), inertial measurement unit (IMU) kinematics, and NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) ratings were derived into a 34 feature vector and classified using four models under Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross Validation to ensure our models were not trained on already seen data. SVM with radial basis kernel reached 89.4% accuracy (AUC = 0.932) on low-risk lifting, Logistic Regression reached 84.8% (AUC = 0.904) on high-risk lifting. NASATLX physical demand proved to be the most important feature in permutation importance, outranking all biomechanical features. Perceived workload may be a more consistent cross-subject signal than objective biomechanics, with practical implications for low-burden field evaluation.

items.title: Non-Linear Analysis and Optimization of Weight and Center of Mass for AR Glasses Wear Comfort
items.abstract: This article investigates the effects of weight and Center of Mass (CoM) of AR glasses on subjective assessment during wearing tasks. Utilizing a modular prototyping system, 100 participants evaluated 20 weight-CoM configurations. To address the limitations of linearized Likert scale data, this study constructed a hybrid analytical framework incorporating Generalized Estimating Equations, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with SHAP explanations, and Polynomial Response Surface Methodology. The results revealed significant non-linear coupling effects of weight and CoM on comfort and established a quantitative engineering mapping model based on ordinal data analysis. Furthermore, SHAP analysis identified dynamic stability and nasal comfort as the two most influential perceptual dimensions, jointly accounting for 79.2% of the total SHAP importance. Accordingly, this study proposes engineering optimization guidelines for AR glasses, providing a quantitative basis for lightweighting and weight-distribution optimization of wearable devices.

items.title: Occupational Hazards Associated with Pig Production in Southern Senatorial District of Cross River State, Nigeria
items.abstract: The study examined occupational hazards common among pig farmers and workers in the Southern Senatorial District of Cross River State, Nigeria. The research was guided with four research purposes and questions, and three hypotheses. Survey design was adopted and farm owners, workers and farm owners’ families constituted the population for the study. A sample of hundred and twenty (120) respondents was drawn from the seven local government areas that formed the study area, and were administered questionnaire items. Data collected were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential analyses, including chi-squares tests and independent sample t-tests at 0.05 level of significance. The result revealed the socioeconomic characteristics, common associated hazards and health problems experience by the respondents. Economically exposed respondents lost greatly more income due to illness less than their non-exposed counterparts (t = 5.87, p<0.05). Significantly safety training was greatly associated with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) usage (𝑥2 =21.54, p<0.05). The study concludes that pig production in the study area poses substantial occupational health and economic risks. The research recommends among others regular training on safety and zoonosis prevention, sensitization of farmers on safe handling practices and farm hygiene, enaction of policies supporting occupational health surveillance, and establishment of rural health clinics and mobile health outreach for pig farmers.

items.title: Occupational Health, Safety and Environmental Compliance and its Effects: A Case Study of Federal Polytechnic Bauchi, Nigeria
items.abstract: Occupational Health, Safety and Environmental (OHSE) compliance is a dynamic requirement for ensuring wellbeing, safety at work environments, curtailing work-related hazards and reassuring sustainable institutional procedures. This research evaluates the quality of OHSE compliance and its effects at Federal Polytechnic Bauchi, Nigeria. The study method adopted a cast study involving structured questionnaires, workplace adherences and inspection of safety-related documents. The study emphasized on safety observances, hazard regulatory procedures, personal protective equipment accessibility, emergency enthusiasm and environmental management routines. The findings demonstrate that effective OHSE compliance contributes significantly to accident prevention, better productivity, environmental safety and enhanced institutional sustainability. However, problems such as inadequate safety mindfulness, incoherent monitoring, inadequate safety resources and weak enforcement methods negate full compliance. The research recommends continuous safety training, enhanced inspection protocols, adequate provision of safety facilities (PPE), better-quality waste control systems and stronger institutional OHSE policies to intensify workshop safety and routine.

items.title: Operational and organizational training for managing work stress among police investigation officers: a global perspective
items.abstract: Criminal investigators face chronic demands beyond general police work: repeated analysis of traumatic digital evidence, heavy caseloads, cognitive overload, evidentiary scrutiny, and accountability for error (Schlosser et al., 2024;Strickland et al., 2023;Woodhams and Duran, 2024).Digitalization and rapidly changing technical requirements intensify these pressures while recruitment and retention problems restrict capacity (Drew et al., 2024). Burnout consequently threatens both officer well-being and investigative quality (Bezie et al., 2024).The literature separates operational stressors, which are intrinsic to the work, from organizational stressors, which arise from how the institution is run, such as workload allocation, supervisory support, role clarity, and culture (Gavin and Porter, 2024). A finding that is decisive for training design is that organizational and operational stressors, rather than trauma exposure alone, predict most stressrelated outcomes among investigative and forensic staff (Keech and Drew, 2026;Porter and Gavin, 2025). Among United States investigators exposed to CSAM, the frequency of exposure was not systematically related to mental health, apart from violent material, which was linked to elevated posttraumatic stress; agency-level factors such as control over workload, debriefing, and feedback on case outcomes were what mitigated harm (Mitchell et al., 2023). This Opinion draws on peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2026, identified through database searches on police and investigator occupational stress, psychological capital, technostress, and organizational interventions, prioritizing evidence specific to investigative and forensic roles and using the broader occupational-health literature where role-specific studies are scarce. On that basis, I argue that stress-management interventions for investigators should rest on two complementary pillars. Operational training strengthens the adaptive capacity of the individual officer; organizational training reshapes the leadership, climate, and work systems in which officers operate (Figure 1). Current practice still leans heavily toward the first pillar, locating both the problem and its remedy in the worker. I treat investigator resilience as a structurally enabled resource rather than a fixed personal trait. The evidence supports a structural rather than an episodic framing. Multidimensional assessments show that police stress tracks enduring features of the work environment, including job demands, control, support, role clarity, and organizational change, more than isolated critical incidents (Strukcinskiene et al., 2025). Within investigative and forensic units, organizational and operational demands, not trauma exposure alone, predict the largest share of stress-related outcomes, while supervisor support, peer support, and a positive psychosocial safety climate act as the main buffering resources (Keech and Drew, 2026). This pattern recasts exposure as one demand among several rather than the sole cause of harm (Drew et al., 2024).The job demands-resources (JD-R) model explains how demands deplete well-being unless balanced by resources. Conservation of resources (COR) theory explains how continued depletion without recovery creates loss spirals and burnout (Demerouti et al., 2001;Hobfoll, 1989;Zhou et al., 2024). Operational training adds personal resources; organizational action protects them.Integration requires a multilevel and temporal account. Structural demands such as backlog, traumatic exposure, digital overload and ambiguity first activate the JD-R health-impairment pathway. The two pillars then operate in a reciprocal cycle: operational training may improve immediate regulation, appraisal and help-seeking, while organizational training changes workload, supervisory behaviour, recovery opportunities and psychological safety. These organizational changes determine whether personal gains are replenished or progressively depleted. COR theory therefore predicts that operational training is most useful during acute demand, whereas organizational redesign becomes increasingly important when demands are recurrent, controllable and system-generated. Professional identity is proposed as a mediator, not a presumed protection: stress may weaken identification through cynicism and perceived value conflict, while credible supervision and meaningful feedback may restore identification and its wellbeing benefits. Job security is proposed as a moderator because officers who fear transfer, stigma, career penalty or job loss may be less able to disclose strain or use support. The model predicts that combined interventions will be more durable when workload control, psychological safety and leadership accountability improve; it does not assume that combined interventions will always outperform individual training.Digital transformation adds a further, persistent demand. Technostress, the strain from constant connectivity, information overload, and the intrusion of technology into recovery time, behaves as a chronic job demand associated with lower well-being and burnout, and it is intrinsic to investigative work built around digital evidence (Pansini et al., 2023;Mansuroğlu and Smith, 2026). Two resources deserve emphasis because they locate where interventions should act. Professional identity mediates the link between occupational stress and well-being, and perceived job security moderates it, which indicates that meaning and stability are protective resources shaped largely by organizations rather than by individuals alone (Wu et al., 2025).Operational training targets the officer's own coping repertoire and has a credible evidence base.Mindfulness-based resilience training has shown feasibility and promising effects on stress in police samples (Christopher et al., 2024), and physiologically grounded programs that pair heart-ratevariability biofeedback with metacognitive skill practice are being trialed to build resilience in officers exposed to post-traumatic stress injuries (Andersen et al., 2023). These approaches develop psychological capital, the malleable resources of hope, efficacy, resilience, and optimism that are associated with lower burnout and turnover intention and with higher engagement and performance (Loghman et al., 2023).The limits of a purely individual approach are equally clear, and they should be stated without overclaiming the alternative. Worker-directed interventions place the burden of adaptation on the person, can imply that distress signals personal weakness, and tend to fade once officers return to unchanged conditions. They do not remediate the organizational stressors that the investigatorspecific evidence identifies as the deepest sources of harm (Gavin and Porter, 2024;Mitchell et al., 2023). Teaching investigators to regulate their physiology is useful, but it does not reduce an unmanageable caseload or a dismissive command climate.Comparative reviews suggest that organizational and combined interventions may produce benefits comparable with, and sometimes more durable than, individual interventions in healthcare and general workplaces (Catapano et al., 2023;Dahlqvist et al., 2023). This evidence cannot be treated as direct proof for investigative policing. Its relevance is theoretical and conditional: reducing demands at source should protect recovery, but policing adds hierarchy, operational urgency, confidentiality requirements and occupational stigma. Accordingly, the present framework offers a testable proposition rather than an effectiveness claim. Organizational action should be staged according to readiness, fidelity, leadership commitment and resources, with individual training retained as an accessible component while system-level effects are evaluated.For investigative units, this pillar includes trauma-informed supervision, case-outcome feedback, exposure and caseload review, breaks and recovery after graphic-material work, peer support, psychosocial safety monitoring, and leadership accountability (Mitchell et al., 2022(Mitchell et al., , 2023;;Keech and Drew, 2026). Leadership links the pillars because supportive leadership can strengthen psychological capital (Loghman et al., 2023). Table 1 distinguishes evidence from proposals requiring testing.Delivery should fit agency capacity. National laboratories may use exposure logging, specialist supervision, and rotation; small or rural forces may need regional case-sharing, remote consultation, peer supervision, and referral agreements. Internet-crime task forces may prioritize graphicexposure limits and outcome feedback, while general detective units address backlog, autonomy, and recovery. In lower-resource settings, feasible minimums include workload review, supervisor training, confidential referral, and protected recovery. The functions are transferable, but implementation must reflect staffing, geography, labor protections, culture, and stigma.Implementation barriers require active design responses. Hierarchy can be addressed through confidential reporting routes, supervisor accountability and protected escalation pathways; resource constraints through phased implementation and regional/shared services; stigma through routine, universal wellbeing processes rather than exceptional referral; confidentiality concerns through independent providers and clear data-governance rules; and competing priorities through integrating recovery, exposure review and case-outcome feedback into existing quality and supervision meetings.These strategies are proposed implementation mechanisms, not evidence of established effectiveness. Their value should be assessed using reach, fidelity, acceptability, equity of access and unintended-consequence indicators. Treating barriers as design conditions preserves the structural argument while acknowledging that organizational interventions can fail or impose new burdens if poorly implemented.Table 1. Evidence-calibrated intervention matrix. Indicators are proposed evaluation measures unless directly tested in the cited studies.Equity is a design requirement rather than a descriptive add-on. Access to resilience resources may vary by gender, rank, rurality, contract status, unit type and national capacity (Bezie et al., 2024;Porter and Gavin, 2025). Women officers may encounter additional caregiving demands, gendered expectations or lower psychological safety; junior officers may have less discretion to request recovery; rural officers may face distance, limited specialist services and confidentiality concerns in small teams. These conditions may alter both exposure to demands and the feasibility of each intervention. Implementation should therefore require disaggregated monitoring of reach, uptake, workload relief, perceived safety and outcomes by gender, rank, rurality and unit. Agencies should offer multiple access routes, remote and regional options, protected time, culturally appropriate providers and safeguards against career penalties. Core functions should be retained, but delivery should be adapted and tested rather than assumed to be equivalent across contexts.The pillars are complementary but not interchangeable. Policy should become auditable and equitable. Units should review caseload and graphic exposure regularly; provide confidential, trauma-informed supervision; record access to case-outcome feedback; protect recovery; and monitor climate, absence, turnover intention and support uptake. Universal exposure caps are premature. Agencies should instead define local trigger points for mandatory workload review, document exceptions and test whether thresholds predict health and service outcomes. Senior leaders should be accountable for system indicators alongside case throughput. Every implementation should report reach and effects by gender, rank, rurality, unit type and national context, and should include safeguards against retaliation, disclosure of sensitive case information and unequal access. Where resources are limited, minimum standards should include workload review, trained supervision, confidential referral and protected recovery time, with regional partnerships used to extend specialist access.The framework remains an evidence-informed working hypothesis. Investigator-specific studies identify plausible risks and protective practices, but causal evidence for organizational redesign is limited and evidence from other occupations is not automatically transferable. Agencies should therefore build officer skills, reduce recurrent resource depletion, and evaluate both workforce and investigative outcomes.

items.title: Organizational Performance as A Systemic Construct
items.abstract: This study reconceptualizes organizational performance through the lens of systems thinking, arguing that conventional financial and efficiency-based approaches are increasingly inadequate for capturing the complexity of contemporary organizations. In response, this study develops a systemic conceptualization of performance as a multidimensional and emergent construct. Drawing on classical and contemporary contributions to systems theory, the analysis conceptualizes the organization as a complex sociotechnical system composed of interdependent subsystems embedded within dynamic environments. Within this framework, performance is not treated as a static outcome but as a dynamic property emerging from continuous interactions between internal structures and external conditions. This article examines the evolution of performance theories, from traditional financial models to multidimensional frameworks such as the Competing Values Framework, and discusses contemporary measurement approaches, including the Balanced Scorecard and sustainability-oriented frameworks. It ultimately proposes a systemic conception of performance structured around a viability-performance matrix, emphasizing feedback loops, adaptive capacity, and structural tensions between stability and flexibility. This study contributes to management theory by bridging systems thinking and performance literature, with implications for organizational design, governance, and sustainability-oriented management.

items.title: Parameter Identification and Situation Awareness in Distribution Networks Under Incomplete Information Driven by Data-Physical Fusion
items.abstract: Some distribution networks are characterized by weak grid structures and complex feeder deployment, which leads to missing information such as line parameters. Existing power flow methods depend heavily on accurate parameters and lack sufficient dynamic adaptability, making them unsuitable for incomplete-information conditions. To address this problem, this paper proposes a distribution-network situation-awareness model driven by data-physical fusion. First, to cope with the dual challenges of incompleteness and uncertainty in line parameters, a bounded multi-operating-condition line-parameter identification model is constructed, and the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy is employed to determine line resistances and reactances; the resulting parameters are then used for data augmentation. Next, a situation-awareness model for distribution networks is developed by combining a physics-informed neural network with a mixture-of-experts architecture. In this way, data-driven learning is integrated with physical constraints so that the perceptual capability of deep learning is preserved while the model remains guided by power-flow physics. Finally, the model is validated using the IEEE 33-bus system and historical operating data from an actual distribution area in China. The results show that the proposed model outperforms the comparison methods on the IEEE 33-bus system and effectively tracks multiple state variables in the actual distribution area, supporting its feasibility for incomplete-information conditions.

items.title: Physical and Psychosocial Occupational Hazards Among Solid Waste Collectors in Swali Yenagoa, Bayelsa State
items.abstract: Proper solid waste disposal is vital for public and environmental health, and waste collectors play a central role in maintaining community sanitation. Solid waste collectors experience high rates of injuries such as cuts and musculoskeletal disorders in Africa, largely due to inadequate PPE, poor training, and limited healthcare access. This study is significant because it fills the gap in community-level data on physical and psychosocial occupational hazards among solid waste collectors in Swali, Yenagoa, and providing evidence to improve occupational health and safety practices. The aim of this study was to assess the physical and psychosocial occupational hazards among waste collectors in Swali Community, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State. This research adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The target population comprised of all formal waste collectors in the Swali community who were exposed to physical and psychosocial occupational hazards. A total of 125 waste collectors were selected using a simple random sampling technique. Data was collected through structured questionnaire and observational checklist over a period of seven (7) weeks and analyzed using descriptive statistics with the aid of SPSS version 25. Findings revealed that the most frequently reported physical occupational hazard was cuts or puncture wounds with 44.8% of respondents agreeing and 24.0% strongly agreeing, yielding the highest mean score of 3.67 ± 1.18. Regarding psychosocial hazards, 52% reported experiencing stress due to your job, while 51% reported verbal abuse while working. In conclusion, the study found that waste collectors in Swali, Yenagoa, experience significant physical and psychosocial hazards. It is recommended that PPE compliance policies should be enforced and provision of safe work technique.

items.title: Play-Based Approach: A Strategy in Teaching Number Recognition Among Kindergarteners in Private School
items.abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of a play-centered approach in teaching number recognition among kindergarten learners of Inter-Asia Business Institute Philippines Incorporated during the School Year 2025–2026. Guided by the theories of Vygotsky, Dewey, and Montessori, the research utilized a one-group pretest-posttest design involving fifteen (15) kindergarten learners. The intervention integrated play-based activities such as number games, counting hopscotch, and storytelling to enhance cognitive engagement and numeracy skills. Findings revealed a significant improvement in learners’ posttest scores compared to their pretest performance, as confirmed by the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (p < 0.001). The results indicated that the play-based approach effectively enhanced learners’ number recognition, motivation, and class participation. The study concluded that play-based learning is a powerful instructional method that fosters holistic child development and supports the MATATAG curriculum’s goals of meaningful and enjoyable learning. It recommended broader adoption of play-centered strategies in early childhood education to strengthen foundational numeracy skills.
